b7bvzg7pp7dy.body: This incident has been resolved. Between 12:00 and 12:12 PM PDT on August 26, server-side SDKs establishing new streaming connections experienced elevated error rates. Existing streaming connections were not affected, and polling requests continued to be served with error rates below 1%. Some requests to the LaunchDarkly web application also experienced elevated errors between approximately 11:29 AM and 12:03 PM PDT. The issue was caused by an internal configuration change, which has been reverted. All systems have recovered and are operating normally. No customer data was lost or compromised.
b7bvzg7pp7dy.title: Flag delivery errors in Streaming API

chywwz01ptb0.body:
All service availability has been fully restored.

Customers using server-side SDKs might need to restart their applications to re-enable the SDKs' connection to LaunchDarkly. Customers using the Relay Proxy may also need to restart their Relay Proxy; in this case, the Relay Proxy should be restarted before restarting their applications that connect to it.

To determine if an application needs to be restarted, customers can look at their application logs. Affected SDKs will emit (depending on language) logs containing one of "giving up permanently", "Invalid SDK key", "unauthorized", or "not authorized", or "401". Services which emitted logs such as these before 9:13AM PT may be unable to receive flag updates and will be unable to send events to LaunchDarkly until they are restarted.
chywwz01ptb0.title: Web application unavailable and flag delivery evaluations have elevated failure rate

dfqd9pff4533.body:
Server-side streaming began rejecting new connections across all commercial regions, causing 500/503 errors for customers attempting to establish new SDK streaming connections for a brief period of time.

Detailed timelines of the incident:
- us-east-1 : 7:53 AM  PST to 8:24 AM PST
- ap-southeast-1: 7:53 AM  PST to 7:55 AM PST
- eu-west-1: 7:53 AM  PST to 8:35 AM PST

The team was quickly able to deploy the mitigation before an incident could be declared in our status pages, this is why we're posting it, retroactively.
By 8:35am PST connections were re-established successfully in all commercial regions.
